question: Does the EMB-hosted 2024 Boac River dredging EIS executive summary expose fish-baseline data that can support a named-river species record?

source.title: Executive Summary: Rehabilitation / Improvement of Riverbed and Navigational Sea Channel of Boac River
source.provider: Environmental Management Bureau MIMAROPA Region; Provincial Government of Marinduque; DPWH MIMAROPA; Kyro Builders, Inc.
source.projectLocation: Boac River dredging and navigational-zone project near Barangay Tabigue, Municipality of Boac, Marinduque. The summary describes a 500 m river dredging reach and a separate navigational shoreline area; these are project zones, not a full river boundary.
source.reuseStatus: No open license or item-specific public-app reuse permission was located in the executive summary. No report pages, map, coordinates, tables, or images were copied into app assets.

evidenceReview.monitoringReference: The executive summary proposes periodic environmental monitoring to compare fish and crustacean populations with baseline data, but does not provide the baseline table or its dates, methods, locations, metrics, or vouchers.
evidenceReview.eiaTeamRole: The summary lists a marine biologist assigned to a freshwater and marine ecology baseline assessment. This identifies an EIS workstream, not the contents or quality of an unretrieved full report.
evidenceReview.genericRestockingReference: A mitigation matrix recommends restocking suitable non-invasive fish in undisturbed areas; it does not identify a taxon, prove local native status, or document a fish capture.
evidenceReview.aquacultureReference: Tilapia, pompano, and snappers occur in a mitigation discussion about compliant cage culture and feeding regimens. They are not presented as a wild-capture species list for the Boac River.
evidenceReview.otherFishReferences: Fish fry, fish habitat, fish migration, freshwater prawns, and potential population effects are discussed generically as impact pathways; no taxon-level river observations are provided.
evidenceReview.publicIndexAccess: The EMB public hearing/consultation page returned HTTP 403 in this review. Search-indexed material exposed the executive summary; the full EIS was not retrieved. This bounded result does not establish that the full EIS is unavailable through EMB or the project proponent.

decision.reason: The executive summary confirms that a freshwater/marine ecology assessment was part of the EIS scope but does not expose fish results. Generic impacts, restocking language, and cage-culture species cannot substantiate Boac River wild occurrences.

nextAction: If the full EIS or its aquatic-baseline annex becomes publicly retrievable, screen field dates, fish-sampling methods, named sites, taxon labels, station-to-taxon allocation, voucher identifiers, and item-specific reuse terms before admitting any historical evidence. Until then, keep this as a retrieval lead only.

sources.supports: Official EMB-hosted 28-page executive summary; project location and footprint descriptions; EIA team role for freshwater/marine ecology; generic fish mitigation, aquaculture and monitoring references; no fish-baseline result table.
Official EMB MIMAROPA public hearing index search result names the Boac River project and links its notice and executive summary; direct page access returned HTTP 403 in this review.
